beats.text: Ten minutes on a dating app, and suddenly nobody looks good.
In three studies, singles swiped through profiles. Yes, or no.
The longer they swiped, the less often they said yes.
They also grew less satisfied, and more pessimistic about their own chances.
Researchers call it a rejection mindset.
So if everyone starts looking wrong, it might be the swiping. Not them. Take a break.

sources: Pronk & Denissen (2020). A rejection mind-set: Choice overload in online dating. Social Psychological and Personality Science 11(3). Three studies (n=315, 158, 305), single heterosexual adults 18-30; acceptance rates decreased over the course of the task; satisfaction declined and pessimism about being accepted rose. Via PsyPost.
